premises.name: mixed-order determinant/Brascamp-Lieb Fourier envelope
premises.scope: physical cross-block minor laws with I-side row marginals <=1/2; pointwise envelope derivation valid at mean order 2, with strict mean order >2 previously used only for L1 inversion

result.pair_volume_fourier: For a law Omega on nonzero physical 2x2 minors with I-side row marginals <=1/2, |phi_R(t)|<=min(1,2pi sqrt(e)K_2(Omega)^(-1/4)|t|^-1), integral |phi_R|^(3/2)<=12pi sqrt(e)K_2(Omega)^(-1/4), and ||p_R||_3<=6^(2/3)e^(1/3)K_2(Omega)^(-1/6).
result.natural_pair_volume: For natural pair-volume E2=e2(M^TM), K_2=E2 and q_i=sum_{k!=i}||r_i wedge r_k||^2/E2. If max q_i<=1/2, the full E2 is spent without selecting one physical pair.
result.square_lift: With physical pivot a!=0, ||p_Q||inf<=16(e/3)^(1/4)|a|^-1/2 E2^-1/8 under the diffuse natural-pair hypothesis; essential boundedness only, continuity not proved by this dependent-shift lift.
result.partner_application: Using account02/B01 r31, E2>=alpha Z/||r_h||^2 gives ||p_Q||inf<=15.610374 |a|^-1/2 (||r_h||^2/(alpha Z))^(1/8) whenever the complementary natural pair-volume is diffuse.
result.stress_family: A_r=[1] direct_sum [[0,M_r],[M_r^T,0]] has nonzero spectrum {1,1,1,-1,-1}, E2=1, pair row marginals 1/r, and individual nonzero 2x2 minors r^-2; nevertheless the theorem gives a uniform <15.611 density bound for all admissible product laws.

next_step: If complementary natural e2 is heavy, use the aggregate wedge-hub identity to route to account02/B01 r32 mixed-hub, a two-dimensional random-slope packet, grouped squares/two slopes, or a mean-order>2 mixed-minor law before reciprocal coordinate selection.
